evidence.clarity: 1440 first screen: H1 'Catch the API change before a client team does.' plus lede 'runs your OpenAPI spec against your staging API on every pull request... points to the field, the endpoint and the spec line', with 'Install the GitHub App' and the pricing line right below. As the backend lead whose team just broke a mobile client, I could repeat what it does after one read.
evidence.fit: It covers the explicit asks: both supplied destinations (5 links each), free/$19 pricing in the hero, the Postman and bug-report replacement in 'Find out on the pull request, not from a bug report', and staging-only in 'It reads staging. Never production.' The staging-only reassurance only appears about 4 screens down, though, and is missing from the hero, where a lead deciding in two minutes first doubts it. The team lead who approves gets one line, 'easy to put in front of whoever approves it', plus a calculator. API platform teams get no path of their own.
evidence.distinctiveness: The failing-check card with a side-by-side 'Spec expects / Staging returned' diff comes from the product. The rest is a familiar dev-tool template: a three-card 'Three ways a response drifts' grid, a numbered 'How it runs' list, a Today vs With comparison, two pricing cards and a CTA band. Inter-style type on a grey-blue background.
evidence.proof: 1440: the whole failing check is in view without scrolling: 'contractcheck / staging failed: 3 responses don't match openapi.yaml', commit, '43 of 46 operations matched', and an expanded diff of the missing currency field with 'openapi.yaml line 214'. I expanded 'Changed type' (amount_due "4190" vs integer, line 388) and 'Undocumented status' (409 vs 201/400/404, line 512), and toggled 'After the fix', which showed 46 of 46 and a passing list. This answers 'what does a failing check look like' very well. It is a fixed two-state example: I can't try my own response.
evidence.craft: Clean, consistent spacing and type at 1440, 768 and 390, and no overflow (probe 0px). The card's diff panes are legible. Minor issues: the two smallest text elements are 11.88px, the passing view's right-column notes are faint grey, and the lower sections read as a uniform stack of bordered boxes.
evidence.mobile: 390: there is no menu. 'How it works' and 'Pricing' are hidden and only 'Docs' and 'Install' stay in the header, so section navigation is lost. The card starts about halfway down the first screen. The Failing/After the fix buttons are 30px tall and the stepper buttons 38px, both under 44px. The 'An example run' caption sits at y≈1496, below the whole card, two screens down. The page stacks correctly with no horizontal scroll.
evidence.honesty: No invented customers or numbers, and the pricing matches the brief. But the example label is a caption under the card ('An example run. Endpoints and values are illustrative.'), not at the top. At 390 it is about 1,000px below where the example's '43 of 46 operations matched / Ran in 38s' first appear. The CTA 'Install the GitHub App' says exactly where it goes.
evidence.interaction: All three failure rows expand and collapse with aria-expanded updated. The Failing/After the fix toggle swaps views. Calculator: + and − work and the total updates live. '0' and '-5' silently clamp to 1 ($19), '1000' clamps to 999 ($18,981), '2.5' snaps to 3, and empty shows no message. That is defensible but has no explanation. 0 console errors at all widths. The demo is a canned two-state view.
evidence.copy: Specific and in the engineer's vocabulary: 'A refactor drops a property from a serializer', 'The Postman collection that would have caught it hasn't been run since spring', 'Fix the handler or update the spec, then push.' No buzzwords. Some repetition between the hero card, the three rule cards and How it runs (the same three failure types explained three times).
evidence.first_screen: 1440: a specific promise, a full failing check that makes it believable, and an action that names its destination ('Install the GitHub App'), all in one viewport. 390: the promise, CTA and pricing are in view and only the top of the check (title, commit, first 'Missing field' row) shows. Staging-only is absent from the first screen at both widths.

problems: The staging-never-production reassurance, the security doubt a backend lead has before granting a GitHub App, is not in the hero and appears only about 4 screens down.
The example label is a caption below the card; at 390 it is about two screens below the sample's numbers ('43 of 46 operations matched', 'Ran in 38s').
390: no menu (section links hidden), segmented toggle 30px and stepper 38px targets, and the rest of the page after the card is a long stack of similar bordered boxes.

evidence.clarity: The H1 'Expected number. Got string.' is a hook in my own language rather than a statement of the product. The very next line fixes that: 'Contractcheck is a GitHub App for backend teams. On every pull request it runs your OpenAPI spec against your staging API, and fails the check when a response stops matching the spec.' What, who and next step are all clear before scrolling, at 1440 and at 390.
evidence.fit: Every ask is met, each with a deliberate place on the page. The hero line says 'It reads responses from your staging API only, never production', and there is a full 'Staging only' section with Q&A ('Does it touch production? No.'). The calculator is titled 'What the team lead approves', which serves the approver. A setup section shows a labelled example .github/contractcheck.yml shape, which is what a lead installing on one repo wants to see. The Postman line is answered directly. Both supplied URLs are used throughout. Tone is dry and engineer-to-engineer.
evidence.distinctiveness: The page is built around a check-sheet motif: a 'FAILED'/'PASSED' rubber stamp, condensed headline type, monospace JSON pointers, a two-lane 'Today / With Contractcheck' track ending in 'Bug report: total is a string now?', and a 'NEVER' stamp on the production node. It is recognisable without the logo. The stamp is borderline decorative, but it carries the pass/fail state.
evidence.proof: 1440 first screen: a 'SAMPLE' bar, then 'contractcheck / staging', 'Pull request #214 · Refactor order serializer', '3 problems in 2 responses, checked against openapi.yaml', and the Missing field and Type changed rows with JSON-pointer locations. I clicked 'Add currency back' (2 problems), 'Send total as a number' (1 problem) and 'Document 409 in the spec' (stamp flips to PASSED, 'No problems. Both responses match openapi.yaml'). I also edited the response body myself, which makes it a working check rather than a picture. A's static diff (spec line number, side by side) is slightly closer to a real check output.
evidence.craft: Deliberate type scale, a consistent dashed-rule rhythm inside the sheet, and no overflow at 320, 390, 768 or 1440 (probe 0px, smallest text 12px, axe empty). Minor issues: the JSON pointers wrap awkwardly ('#/paths/~1orders~1{id}~1cancel/post/responses' breaks over 3 lines at 1440), and at 1440 'Reset the sample' falls just below the fold (y=936).
evidence.mobile: 390: the Menu button opens a full-width list with an Install button. Escape closes it, and tapping 'Pricing' scrolled to the section and closed the menu. All visible targets are 44px or taller (none under 44 measured). The SAMPLE label and FAILED stamp are in the first screen. Tapping 'Add currency back' rewrites that row in place to 'FIXED... currency is back' with the button turned to 'Undo'. But when the last fix makes the check pass, the verdict line is about 265px above the viewport, so the PASSED stamp is not visible where I tapped.
evidence.honesty: The label comes first at every width: a black 'SAMPLE check run on an example spec, simulated in your browser' bar at the top of the card, and 'Example spec, requests and responses written for this page' at the bottom. The config file is captioned 'Example of the shape. The docs have the real file name and keys.' The step-3 strip carries its own 'SAMPLE' tag. No invented customers, timings or counts. Pricing and staging-only claims match the brief.
evidence.interaction: Every fix button toggles to 'Undo' and back, and the problem count and response count update correctly (3/2, 2/2, 1/1, 0). 'Reset the sample' restores 3 problems. In the editable body: empty gives 'Empty body' and the field rows switch to 'Not checked'; '{"id": 5' gives 'Not JSON' with the parse position; '[1,2]' gives 'spec expects an Order object. Staging sent an array'; null status and numeric currency are each listed as Type changed. Calculator: empty gives '—' with 'Enter how many...'; -5, 1000 and 2.5 give 'Enter a whole number from 0 to 999'; 0 gives '$0, Public repositories only'. A live region announces each change. 0 console errors.
evidence.copy: Specific and consistent: 'Expected number. Got string.', 'Serializer changed; reviewers read the diff', 'The Postman collection that was meant to catch this only works when someone remembers to run it', 'Make the next breaking response fail a check, not a client.' Buttons say what they do ('Add currency back', 'Document 409 in the spec'). The staging-only point is repeated three or four times, which is a little much.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: the hook, a one-line definition, 'Install the GitHub App', price and staging-only line, plus a SAMPLE failing check with two problems all fit in one viewport. 390: the promise, CTA, price/staging line, SAMPLE bar and FAILED header are visible, but the first problem row is only at the bottom edge. The headline is a symptom rather than an outcome.

problems: 390: completing the last fix flips the verdict to PASSED about 265px above the viewport, so the main state change happens out of sight (only the row text and a screen-reader announcement change near the tap).
The headline 'Expected number. Got string.' is a hook, not an outcome statement; the promise depends on the subhead.
The sample's JSON-pointer locations wrap into ragged 3-line fragments, and the staging-only message is repeated in hero, hero footer, section and closing band.

reason: As the backend lead, I get my two first doubts answered in B's hero: the staging-only line is there, and the sample check is labelled. I can also break and fix B's sample response myself, see the config shape and price my repos for the approver. That makes installing on one repo an easy yes. A's static spec-vs-staging diff with line numbers is arguably the more realistic picture of a failing check. If the buyer cared only about seeing a realistic check output, and not about the production-access doubt, A would be close.
